name: Sega Master System
description: Sega's 8-bit console, released in Japan as the Mark III in 1985 and redesigned as the Master System for the West. It lost badly to the NES in Japan and North America but did well in Europe and especially Brazil, where Tectoy kept making it for decades.

specs.sound: SN76489 PSG in VDP; YM2413 FM on JP model

curiosities: It had a slot for credit-card-sized Sega Card games as well as cartridges.
The SegaScope 3-D Glasses used LCD shutters to create a stereoscopic image.
Later models had games such as Alex Kidd in Miracle World built in.
The Japanese Master System included a built-in FM sound chip.
story: Sega's SG-1000 had lost to the Famicom, so it built the Mark III in 1985, then restyled it as the Master System for the West in 1986.

It was technically stronger than the NES but Nintendo's licensing kept most publishers away, and in North America it struggled. In Europe, and above all in Brazil, where Tectoy built and sold it for decades, it was a great success. Alex Kidd, Phantasy Star, Wonder Boy III and the 8-bit Sonic games were its stars.
Its hardware lived on almost unchanged in the Game Gear, and Tectoy still sells Master Systems with games built in.
